messages:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired for service=redwood-inference-queue, severity=P1 — symptom=queue_backlog_exhaustion. queued_count=120000, processing_latency_p99 rising. link=https://pagerduty.local/incidents/PD12345

PagerDuty: Initial escalation -> paging Alex (oncall) and Maya (SRE). Autoresolve=off.

Alex (oncall): ack — I'm looking. @Maya can you join? what's the region? :eyes:

Maya (SRE): on it, pulling metrics. early glance: region=us-west-2. queued by route: /embeddings ~90k, /generate ~20k. throughput per pod looks healthy for those that are running.

Devin (infra): logs from autoscaler: failed to provision new GPU nodes, cloud error "quotaExceeded/insufficient_skus" for gpu-instance-family. HPA is healthy but pods pending due to node scheduling.

Alex (oncall): copy. I'll try manual nodegroup scale while we confirm quota.

Alex (oncall): running manual scale now:
```bash
# scale dedicated gpu pool by +8
kubectl scale nodegroup rgp-dedicated --replicas=+8 --namespace=infra || true
```

Maya (SRE): seeing provisioning events — some nodes provisioning, others failing with "insufficient_skus". average queue TTL=45s and increasing.

Devin (infra): manual quota request to cloud is slow. spinning up short-term fallback: deploy quantized-int8 model to cpu fleet and route low-priority traffic there. will need ~10m.

Alex (oncall): plan: 1) try manual scale 2) route non-authenticated / bulk requests to fallback CPU quantized model 3) temporarily reduce batch_size on gen endpoints to lower memory pressure 4) call out to support for customers.

Alex (oncall): applying quick routing change:
```yaml
# traffic override - route non-critical traffic to model-small-cpu
route_override:
  match: {path_prefix: "/bulk", auth: false}
  to: model-small-cpu-v1
```

Maya (SRE): scaled pool +6 nodes successfully. provisioning shows 4 nodes active, 2 failed. failed nodes show sku errors.

Devin (infra): deploying fallback group: az-fast-cpu-pool x6, pushing quantized image redwood/model-gen-int8:latest. kicking autoscaler for that pool.

Sasha (support): preparing customer-facing note. any ETA on stabilization?

Alex (oncall): ETA 15-20m for fallback routing to absorb low-priority load. Will update in 10.

Maya (SRE): noticed traffic spike origin — single client subnet 10.11.0.0/16 producing burst of small requests. recommend temporary WAF throttle/block to relieve queue.

Devin (infra): applied WAF rule: block 10.11.0.0/16 for 10m. traffic dropped ~30% immediately.

PagerDuty: Incident acknowledged by Alex (oncall). Escalation paused.

Alex (oncall): confirmed queue dropping: 120k -> 45k in 6m after WAF + fallback starts. still above baseline but trending down. keeping P1 open.

Maya (SRE): lowering HPA target CPU from 70% -> 50% to spur more pod replicas in available node pool. Applying now.

Alex (oncall): good call. also toggled gen endpoints batch_size from 32 -> 8 to reduce memory footprint.

Sasha (support): posting initial update in #customers: "Investigating infrastructure issue causing elevated latencies for API calls. Mitigations in progress, no data loss. We'll follow up within 30 minutes."

Alex (oncall): handing off primary watch to Maya — I'll be offline in 25m. @Maya please continue monitoring PD12345, create internal incident ticket and assign postmortem to eng-runtime.

Maya (SRE): ack. creating incident ticket PD12345-TKT now and assigning to eng-runtime owners @Devin and @Nora. collecting timeline and logs.

Alex (oncall): TL;DR for the record: root cause appears to be cloud SKU/quota preventing autoscaler from provisioning GPU nodes causing pods to be Pending and queue to build. Mitigations: manual scale (partial), WAF throttle on abusive subnet, fallback routing to CPU quantized model, lowered HPA target, batch_size reduction. Next steps: emergency quota request, full postmortem, improve autoscaler retry/backoff and prewarm pools for safety.

IncidentBot: Incident updated: severity=P1, impact=hosted API latency and backlog. followup: postmortem_requested.

Sasha (support): :thumbsup: will keep customers updated.

Maya (SRE): monitoring alerts set, will update thread with final status and handoff notes.

Alex (oncall): thanks all — leaving handoff notes and runbook references in the PD incident.

Devin (infra): creating quota ticket with cloud support and attaching provisioning failure logs. keeping oncall looped.

Nora (runtime): looping in runtime team for postmortem. can look at autoscaler heuristics and prewarm behavior in next sprint.

Maya (SRE): last check: queue at ~18k and declining. leaving continuous monitors. last update to customers in 20m.

IncidentBot: PagerDuty: incident PD12345 status=monitoring.
